actions.description: Take the plugin's bounded wall-time lapse lock with the upstream method default horizon of 1 s; this pauses the plugin loop that steps the paused Gazebo world and exchanges packets with ArduPilot SITL, not ArduPilot itself, and the plugin clears the lock automatically when the timer expires
actions.name: take_lapse_lock

actions.description: Release this driver's lapse lock; succeeds only when the returned holder count is zero, because a positive count means another holder still pauses the loop
actions.name: release_lapse_lock

facts.text: The plugin is a Gazebo WorldPlugin registered with GZ_REGISTER_WORLD_PLUGIN.
ROS_NAMESPACE is defined as /fdmUDP.
The plugin opens its ROS NodeHandle with ROS_NAMESPACE.
The plugin advertises the relative take_apm_lapseLock service on its /fdmUDP node handle.
The plugin advertises the relative release_apm_lapseLock service on its /fdmUDP node handle.
The TakeApmLapseLock service request has a process_id string and a float32 max_duration; the response has an int32 nb_holders.
The ReleaseApmLapseLock service request has a process_id string; the response has an int32 nb_holders.
The take service calls take_lapseLock(req.max_duration) and returns _nbHolders_lapseLock.
The release service calls release_lapseLock() and returns _nbHolders_lapseLock.
take_lapseLock sets the lock to the requested duration when it is longer than the current one and increments the holder counter.
release_lapseLock decrements the holder counter and clears the lock when no holders remain.
check_lapseLock subtracts loop_elapsed_dt from a held lock and, when the lock falls below zero, sets the lock and the holder count to zero and logs that the simulation resumes.
The loop passes check_lapseLock the loop duration measured with ros::WallTime.

While check_lapseLock returns false the loop continues to its next iteration; otherwise it calls receive_apm_input and, when a servo packet arrived, steps Gazebo unless _isSimPaused is set and sends the FDM state.
init_gazebo_side pauses the Gazebo world.
step_gazebo_sim advances the world with Step(1); its comment says the simulation must be in pause mode for Step to work.
on_gazebo_control toggles _isSimPaused on every world_control pause message and calls SetPaused(true) only when the toggle pauses.
The Cessna spawn launch file includes gazebo_ros empty_world.launch with paused set to true.
MAX_LAPSE_LOCK_ON_MODEL_INSERT is defined as 5 s.
load_parachute_model inserts the parachute model and takes the lapse lock with MAX_LAPSE_LOCK_ON_MODEL_INSERT.
on_parachute_model_loaded sets _loop_lapseLock to 0 without touching the holder count when the parachute model is not found.
on_parachute_model_loaded calls release_lapseLock after attaching the parachute.
receive_apm_input passes the parachute servo value to check_parachute_cmd.
check_parachute_cmd returns for a servo value below 0.5 and otherwise loads the parachute model once.
The recorder camera plugin's lapse-lock service clients target /fdmUDP/take_apm_lapseLock and /fdmUDP/release_apm_lapseLock.
The recorder camera plugin's OnNewFrame, when it saves frames or video, calls its TakeApmLapseLock client with max_duration 5 before and its ReleaseApmLapseLock client after handling the frame.
cessna.xacro leaves its recorder_camera instance inside a comment.
The header states the lapse lock has no memory or identification of holding processes, can resume before a holder has finished, and is a bounded wall-time pause.
The model name defaults to iris.
The plugin reads the SDF UAV_MODEL element into _modelName.
The LFLY Cessna world sets UAV_MODEL to cessna.
LFLY_world_cessna.launch includes cessna_spawn.launch with the LFLY Cessna world.
empty_world_cessna.launch includes cessna_spawn.launch with the empty_world_cessna world.
The empty_world_cessna world loads the plugin without a UAV_MODEL element.
NB_SERVOS_MOTOR_SPEED is defined as 4, commented '4(iris) or 5(cessna)'.
_cmd_motor_speed is declared with NB_SERVOS_MOTOR_SPEED entries and commented as the local copy of the motor speed command in rad/s; _modelName is the next member.
The plugin reads the SDF NB_SERVOS_MOTOR_SPEED element into _nbMotorSpeed.
The LFLY Cessna world sets NB_SERVOS_MOTOR_SPEED to 5.
The aircraft plugin stores motor_speed entries 0 to 4 as the aileron, elevator, propeller (divided by 10), rudder and flap commands.
The aircraft plugin's command indices are Aileron 0, Elevators 1, Propeller 2, Rudder 3 and Flap 4.
UpdatePIDs turns the stored aileron, elevator and rudder commands into angles about the value 500, the flap command into an angle from 0 and the propeller command into a throttle of command / 1000.
The aircraft plugin connects OnUpdate to the world-update-begin event, and OnUpdate calls UpdatePIDs whenever simulation time has advanced.
The plugin advertises mav_msgs/CommandMotorSpeed on /<modelName>/command/motor_speed with queue size 10.
The Cessna aircraft plugin subscribes to the resolved /cessna/command/motor_speed topic.
The plugin includes the generated mav_msgs/CommandMotorSpeed header.
The published CommandMotorSpeed sets frame_id to quad, stamps the current ROS time and fills motor_speed with the configured number of _cmd_motor_speed entries.
receive_apm_input writes each of the first _nbMotorSpeed servo values times 1000 into _cmd_motor_speed and sets every entry to 5, commented as rad/s, when none exceeds 1.
The servo packet comment states each servo value ranges from 0 (no rotation) to 1 (full throttle).
The loop calls receive_apm_input only after check_lapseLock returns true.
receive_apm_input calls publish_commandMotorSpeed only after a complete servo packet is received.
MAX_LAPSE_LOCK_DEFAULT is defined as 1 s.
take_lapseLock's default argument is MAX_LAPSE_LOCK_DEFAULT.
The repository LICENSE.md says the plugin is licensed under Apache v2.0 terms.
The plugin package.xml gives its licence as TODO.
SocketAPM.cpp carries a GNU GPL version 3 or later notice and names Socket.cpp of the ArduPilot project as its source.
The plugin library is built from the plugin sources including src/SocketAPM.cpp.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no Gazebo step, ArduPilot SITL process, UDP socket or wall-clock pacing; placeholder motor speeds do not establish a trajectory or state hash

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free recording fake for the ArduPilot SITL Gazebo ROS surface (no physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free rosbridge handler: it answers the declared subscription and services and records the outbound requests, but it runs no Gazebo world, ArduPilot SITL, UDP bridge, physics step, sensor plugin or wall-clock loop
the plugin's 2.5 ms SITL step (STEP_SIZE_FOR_ARDUPILOT) and its loop rates are source facts, not the fake's timing; the fake has no timestep or pacing
the fake keeps its placeholder lapse lock held until the release service or a test resets it; it does not run the upstream elapsed-wall-time expiry in check_lapseLock

the fake publishes a placeholder motor-speed array only in reply to a subscription; the real plugin publishes only after receiving a SITL servo packet, so a live deployment needs the operator's Gazebo world, ArduPilot SITL and rosbridge
the fake does not model UDP servo packets, FDM replies, Gazebo stepping, sensors, the parachute path, rotor dynamics or the aircraft_plugin consumers
the fake does not model the upstream holder-counter bug or an early resume; a live holder-count race remains unverified

review: the frozen world depends on Gazebo staying paused between the plugin's Step(1) calls; the clone does not stop another client (the Gazebo GUI, a gazebo_ros pause/unpause caller) from unpausing it, and in a running world the aircraft plugin keeps applying the last stored command at every world update while the lock withholds new SITL commands

review: the lock is cleared by any release that brings the shared holder count to zero, including a holder whose own lock already expired (expiry zeroes the count), the plugin's parachute path (a 5 s take released after the model loads) and the recorder camera plugin when it saves frames; a failed parachute load zeroes the lock directly without changing the count

review: the take is not idempotent (every call adds a holder) and the e-stop and the take action succeed only when nb_holders is exactly 1 (the binding grammar has no lower-bound test); a reviewer probe showed one take for an idle e-stop and none on reset, but a second e-stop while latched, an e-stop within 1 s of an ordinary take, another holder or a lost take response make the e-stop report SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED although the loop is paused, and every background retry of the SDK then takes the lock again until a reset, so resuming needs one release per take

review: the binding matches only the LFLY_world_cessna.launch deployment; the iris launch files and empty_world_cessna.launch load worlds without UAV_MODEL, where the plugin publishes /iris/command/motor_speed (and in empty_world_cessna the Cessna listens on /cessna/command/motor_speed, so it receives no commands)

review: upstream defect at the pin: the LFLY Cessna world sets NB_SERVOS_MOTOR_SPEED to 5, but _cmd_motor_speed has 4 entries, so receive_apm_input and publish_commandMotorSpeed write and read a fifth entry past the array (undefined behaviour; _modelName is the next member); the fifth published value, the Cessna flap command, is not trustworthy

review: the motor_speed entries are servo values times 1000; the upstream comments call them rad/s, but the Cessna aircraft plugin reads them as control-surface and propeller commands, so the output declares no unit

measures.description: Read the latest motor-speed command the plugin published after a SITL servo packet; the read makes a fresh subscription and never returns a cached sample
measures.name: observe_motor_speed

safe_state.description: The acknowledged take_apm_lapseLock service holds the plugin's lapse lock with the maximum float32 horizon, so its loop stops exchanging SITL packets and stops stepping the Gazebo world it keeps paused: the aircraft is frozen while no client unpauses Gazebo. ArduPilot SITL keeps running, and any release that brings the shared holder count to zero resumes the loop, such as one by a holder whose own lock expired or by the parachute path.
